{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Physical exam frequency at every visit is excessive",
      "quote": "Physical Examination |  | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X |  |  |",
      "page": 22,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Physical examination is scheduled at every visit including weekly dosing visits, which is burdensome for patients and staff. The protocol text (6.1.8) only requires brief exams at specific visits, so the schedule is inconsistent with the text.",
      "fix": "Reduce physical exams to only those required by Section 6.1.8 (Screening, EOT, and brief exams at W1D1, W3D1, W7D1, and subsequent injection visits)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Vital signs at every visit adds burden without clear need",
      "quote": "Vital Signsi |  | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X |  |  |",
      "page": 22,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Vital signs are collected at every visit, including all weekly dosing visits. This is a minor burden but could be reduced to align with cemiplimab infusion visits or as clinically indicated.",
      "fix": "Consider limiting vital signs to visits where cemiplimab is administered or as clinically indicated."
    },
    {
      "title": "ECG not shown in Schedule of Activities",
      "quote": "A single standard, 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) will be obtained as specified in the Schedule of Assessments (Table 1).",
      "page": 74,
      "section": "6.1.11 Electrocardiogram",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The Schedule of Activities (Table 1) does not include ECG as a procedure, yet Section 6.1.11 states it will be obtained as specified in the schedule. This is a critical inconsistency that will confuse sites.",
      "fix": "Add ECG to the Schedule of Activities at appropriate visits (e.g., Screening, EOT, and as clinically indicated)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Clinical laboratory assessments not detailed in Schedule of Activities",
      "quote": "Clinical laboratory tests will be performed as specified in the Schedule of Assessments (Table 1).",
      "page": 74,
      "section": "6.1.12 Clinical Laboratory Assessments",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The Schedule of Activities does not list laboratory tests (hematology, chemistry, urinalysis, coagulation, thyroid, etc.) as procedures, making it impossible for sites to know when to collect them.",
      "fix": "Add laboratory assessments to the Schedule of Activities with timing (e.g., Screening, each cycle, EOT)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Adrenal function tests at Screening may be difficult to collect",
      "quote": "At Screening, patients assessed as at risk for adrenal insufficiency should undergo diagnostic tests for ACTH and morning cortisol, and/or high-dose ACTH stimulation test (preferred testing method), if clinically indicated, via local laboratory.",
      "page": 74,
      "section": "6.1.12 Clinical Laboratory Assessments",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "advisory",
      "explanation": "The ACTH stimulation test is time-consuming and may be hard to schedule during the Screening window. The wording 'if clinically indicated' is vague and may lead to inconsistent collection.",
      "fix": "Clarify the criteria for 'at risk' and consider allowing these tests to be done during the Screening window with adequate time."
    },
    {
      "title": "ECOG Performance Status not collected at every visit but may be needed for dosing decisions",
      "quote": "ECOG Performance Status |  | X | X |  | X |  |  |  | X | X | X |  |  |",
      "page": 22,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "ECOG is not collected at W2D1, W4D1, W5D1, W6D1, but it is often required for treatment decisions. This could lead to missing data for dose modifications.",
      "fix": "Consider collecting ECOG at every dosing visit or at least at visits where dose modifications are likely."
    },
    {
      "title": "Adverse Event Monitoring not collected at follow-up visits",
      "quote": "Adverse Event Monitoring |  | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X |  |",
      "page": 22,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "AE monitoring is not listed at 100-Day Follow-up or Posttreatment Follow-up, but AEs should be collected throughout the trial, including follow-up. This is a critical gap.",
      "fix": "Add AE monitoring to 100DFU and PTFU visits."
    },
    {
      "title": "Concomitant Medications not collected at follow-up visits",
      "quote": "Concomitant Medications |  | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X |  |",
      "page": 22,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Concomitant medications are not collected at 100DFU or PTFU, but they should be recorded throughout the trial to assess safety and potential drug interactions.",
      "fix": "Add concomitant medication collection to 100DFU and PTFU visits."
    }
  ]
}
